description: MODULE DESCRIPTION For leaders, executives, entrepreneurs and investors this module is an opportunity to gain an understanding of the unique nature of selling value and to gather leading-edge knowledge that they can immediately apply to their work. Sales executives are faced with many challenges today as they seek to grow their business profitably, four appear to be most important. First, it is difficult to understand the value that customers wish to buy and then communicate this value to them. Second, it is challenging selling value in the face of ever increasing pressure from buyers to reduce price paid. Third, segmenting markets based on value and extracting that value is a challenge. Finally, many firms are challenged by the need to align resources with marketing efforts to best secure value from existing marketing investments. This module will address each of these issues and provide practical and actionable solutions drawn from the best thinking of sales research and practice

title: Leading and Coaching for Breakthrough Performance
description: The aim of this two-day module is to introduce participants to the key theory and principles of coaching conversations as part of leadership. The foundations of a coaching approach are discussed to enable a coaching style of leadership to be added to the leader’s repertoire. This coaching module raises awareness of the best ways of developing potential and achieving behavioural change in self and others. The coaching skills introduced as part of this module are all in service of producing quality meaningful conversations which result in better performance. Gaining an understanding of how people think and feel, how to work with human change, and what approach to take are all critical to success in both performance and engagement in all work environments. Along with the coaching theory participants will be engaged in practical coaching experiential groups to develop their coaching skills. This is a highly interactive module which encourages a high level of participation in the room to maximise the learning experience and practice coaching.

title: Talent Management, Collaboration and Winning
description: This module will assist participants to understand how managing top talent is a common problem and subsequently identify best practices for managing & developing talent within their organizations. As high-performers disproportionately contribute to an organization’s performance and tend to be highly mobile, managing them presents unique challenges. This module will identify a number of techniques that will be beneficial to allow participants both to be effective in their careers, and to successfully develop talent in a managerial capacity. It will allow them to understand that managing talent is not a zero-sum game and one can both motivate the high-performers, whilst encouraging other organizational members.

title: Strategy for Breakthrough Performance
description: This module introduces sales performance as a strategic element in a firm’s competitive toolkit. It will situate the sales function within a firm’s overall growth strategy and introduce the class to current business issues affecting drivers of sustainable growth and high performance. On this basis, it will address the integrated components required for organisations to align their strategy and sales such as: value chain analysis, sales, and marketing alignment, leveraging cross functional teams’ expertise and developing insight selling.

title: Key Financial Decisions
description: This module examines, from a financial perspective, the fundamental question of how shareholder value is increased. The answer that question depends on whether the firm’s Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) exceeds its cost of capital (as identified in Module 2). The module then considers the implications of that finding for the firm’s decisions concerning investment in non-current assets (i.e. discounted cash flow analysis of investment proposals) and in current assets (i.e. investment in and management of working capital). The topics to be covered include: • Net present value (NPV) • Internal rate of return (IRR) • Incorporation of risk and uncertainty into long- term decision making • Frameworks of analysis for maximising shareholder value, • Management of inventory, accounts receivable and accounts payable

title: Driving Profitability: Mastering Revenue and Cost Dynamics for Decision-Making
description: During this module, the tools and techniques associated with the costing and subsequent pricing of products and services will be explored. The module will provide an introductory overview of company and divisional performance metrics which will then be covered in greater detail in Module 4: Key Financial Decisions. Finally, during the module, budgetary processes will be investigated. The topics to be covered include: • Direct and indirect costs; • Cost behaviours- variable and fixed costs • Overhead allocation and absorption costing • Activity based costing and value chain analysis • Costing for decision making purposes; relevant vs. sunk costs; • Cost Volume Profit (CVP) analysis • Pricing decisions and target costing • Dealing with risk and uncertainty in decision making • Budgetary control and variance analysis • Incremental vs. zero based budgeting; • Behavioural aspects of the budgeting process; • Performance measurement including key performance indicators • Non-financial performance metrics and the balanced scorecard. • Transfer Pricing

title: International Financial Strategy
description: This module will help participants to understand the impact of the international environment on financial decisions. The module will outline international asset markets and their impact on financing and investment. The nature and use of derivatives as a risk mitigation device will also be examined. The module will review the international monetary system and the Eurozone in particular. Interest rate and especially exchange rate risk will be evaluated. The module will explore the impact of exchange rates on both the competitive position and corporate balance sheets. For example, why are some Eurozone firms more likely to be adversely affected by a 10% decline in Sterling than others? Derivatives including forwards, futures, options and swaps will be carefully explained and the principal determinants of derivative prices will be explored. We will examine ways to hedge and offset different risks. The module will detail the appropriate use of derivatives to mitigate foreign currency risks. We will examine decision making in an international setting evaluating alternative investment opportunities.

title: Strategic Capital Management: Optimizing Debt and Equity for Growth
description: This module explores the importance of establishing a firm’s optimal capital structure in maximising shareholder returns and examines the different equity and debt capital financing options which are appropriate during a firm’s business life cycle. The module develops in students an understanding of how to identify, evaluate and select the optimal capital structure using the appropriate sources and types of financing options including the fixed income market options. The module also provides students with an understanding of the bank lenders credit risk assessment criteria which banks use when credit risk assessing a capital raising proposal and an overview of the financing landscape in Ireland. The topics to be covered include: • The different types and characteristics of equity finance and short- term, medium-term and long-term debt finance • The different sources of raising long term finance including capital markets, bank finance, venture capital, initial public offering, private placements, angel investor market • The equity gap in early-stage firms • Market quotes interpretation regarding stocks • Bonds and derivatives • Optimal financing decisions including theories of capital structure, cost of capital, weighted average cost of capital and the time value of money • Banks credit risk appetite statements and the implications for raising debt finance, credit facility pricing for risk, credit risk assessing capital raising business plans from the bank lender perspective and the different types of security offered

title: Financial Analysis for Strategic Decisions
description: This module will develop the participant’s ability to use financial statements to better understand a firm’s (or business unit’s) strategy, performance, risks and prospects. In particular, the module develops the participant’s ability to use financial accounting information for business decisions and to fully engage with business discussions about that information. An emphasis will be placed on understanding the link between a business’s operations and strategy, and financial accounting information.

title: Mergers & Acquisitions
description: The objectives of this module are to enable participants: • to understand and manage ‘agency problems’ through effective corporate governance, performance related pay and other arrangements. • to evaluate mergers and acquisitions (‘M&A’), including the valuation of target companies and synergies, and the structuring of consideration. • to appreciate the typical responsibilities and challenges facing finance functions within organisations, and the foundations required for the department to deliver the value-adding services discussed within this Diploma.

title: InternationalGlobalNetworkWeek
description: Each year a number of MBA Global Immersion Week modules are offered to UCD MBA students as part of UCD Smurfits involvement with the Global Network for Advanced Management. One module is offered by UCD Smurfit with other modules being offered by our international partner schools. These interactive and immersive modules expose students who chose to participate in them to contemporary issues facing the countries in which the schools offering them are located. These strategic issues are discussed and implications for regions, countries, economies and companies are identified.

title: Application in the Workplace
description: The module equips students to apply the theory of coaching to the workplace. It presents approaches to key issues of practice, such as contracting, supervision, organisational dynamics and ethics.

title: Systems Thinking & Dynamics
description: This module focuses on the team coach taking a systemic approach to their work to allow the team to be aware of and to work with systems within and outside the team. It also focuses on the impact of the system on the team, team members and team coach.

title: Team Coaching Interventions
description: This module focuses on team dynamics – how to spot them, their impact and how to work with them. A wider review of team coaching interventions in general and key principles in design and delivery is also included.

title: Introduction to Team Coaching
description: This module focuses on the science of team effectiveness in order to provide participants with an understanding of what constitutes team outcomes and which processes and inputs have been shown by research to impact team effectiveness. This grounding will assist the team coach in focusing their approach and building rigor and measurement into their work. The importance and complexities of contracting with teams is also explored along with the role of diagnostics as a first key intervention into the team system. Types of team diagnostic approaches will be discussed and key instruments reviewed.

title: Team Coach Models & Approaches
description: Distinction/Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) This module will address key models and processes from the practice and research of team coaching. Team coaching competencies will also be reviewed. Best practice in debriefing the diagnostic data will be discussed with a focus on participants preparing to debrief with their teams.

title: Building Your Team Coaching Practice
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) During this module, participants will complete a deep dive into a leading team diagnostic survey tool for use with their future clients. Participants will also be asked to present their own signature approach to team coaching based on their learnings throughout the programme.

title: Leading in a PSF
description: This module is designed to enable participants to identify and develop the habits of effective leadership and to provide participants with the skills to grow as leaders. Participants will identify how they process information and make decisions and how this impacts others. They will also explore how they impact others through normal day-to-day, work-related behaviours and the importance of receiving and delivering feedback. The module will cover the following themes-- • Identifying and developing the habits of effective leadership; • Leadership challenges in a professional services firm; • Leadership and culture; • Understanding the difference between managing and leading; • How conflict arises in organisations, the role of conflict, as well as the tactics used to resolve inter-personal conflict, with the aim of enhancing participants' conflict resolution techniques; • To be a good leader you need to be a good follower; • The importance of managing oneself; • The impact and importance of emotional intelligence; • The interaction between initiative and leadership; • The importance of motivation; • The importance of teamwork and collaboration in leadership.

title: Delivering with Impact
description: This module is designed to enable participants to enhance their skills as communicators and to develop a confident and capable presenting style. This module will cover the following themes- • Presenting with purpose, presence and confidence; • Connecting with the audience/listener; • Using language and messages that are appropriate to the listener and situation; • Developing physical and vocal habits that enhance personal presence and impact; • Listening skills: staying present, responsive and reactive; • Understanding your personal brand; • Effective communication for critical and difficult situations.

title: Deal Drivers
description: The purpose of this module is to provide participants with a broader, client-aligned perspective designed to enhance their value as business advisory and transaction lawyers. The module aims to set out the key drivers of how and why business deals are done and the role of lawyers and other professional advisers in those deals. This module will cover the following themes- • An overview of the key drivers of corporate M&A activity and property transactions; • An overview of the factors that influence the process of acquiring or off-loading a business; • Pricing a deal; • Paying for a deal; • Due diligence; • Market conditions that might influence a decision about how to proceed; • Motives in M&A growth; • Why deals succeed and fail; • The key role a lawyer plays in deals and what makes a good A&L Goodbody deal lawyer

title: Corporate Dynamics
description: The purpose of this module is to provide participants with a broad understanding of boardroom dynamics, company ownership and control, and how corporates govern themselves. This module will cover the following themes- • Stakeholder issues arising with minority and majority shareholders; • Negative influences on corporate dynamics; • Features and differences between the executive and non-executive board; • The role of the non-executive director and factors which most influence non-executive director perspectives and behaviour; • Shareholder activism and board accountability; • How PLCs prepare for AGMs; • Considerations in preparation of the Annual Report will be discussed.

title: Negotiation
description: This module is designed to enable participants to identify the underlying structure and dynamics of negotiations and to adopt successful strategies for effective negotiation. This module will cover the following themes- • Identification of the dynamics of a negotiation; • The importance of preparing a negotiation strategy; • How to apply value-creating strategies to deliver “win-win” outcomes; • How to execute a negotiation strategy in a live, dynamic negotiation; • Negotiation styles and tactics; • How to negotiate to meet one’s own interests while sustaining business relationships; • Dealing with negotiation challenges; • Building trust and rapport with negotiation counterparts; • The importance of listening skills during a negotiation; • Managing hostility and other emotional issues; • How to remain calm and objective during a difficult negotiation; • Ethical issues in negotiations; • Agents in negotiations; • Multiparty and organisational negotiations.

title: Strategic Mgmt of a PSF
description: The purpose of this module is to provide participants with a broad understanding of the concepts and integrated frameworks for developing and implementing strategy within the firm and for client businesses. The module will allow participants to gain an insight into the practical application of strategy development and implementation. This module will cover the following themes- • What is strategy? • Mission, Vision, Values and the significance of aspirational statements to strategy; • The link between strategy and culture; • Technology and how machine learning and AI will disrupt the business models of PSFs, particularly law firms; • Strategy in the new economy; • Managing innovation and the barriers to innovation within a PSF; • The key dimensions of strategic choice that all firms must make; • Competitor intelligence; • How to develop strategy; • Execution of strategy; • Personal role in strategy • Managing the client portfolio from a strategic perspective.

title: Leading & Dev Client Rel
description: This module is designed to enable participants to effectively lead client relationships and to provide them with the skills to grow and develop those relationships. This module will cover the following themes- • Introduction to the SCOPE client relationship model; • An examination of the A&L Goodbody client relationship and growth approach; • The role of the lawyer in transactions; • Strategic client relationship management; • Understanding and developing effective and efficient client relationships; • Developing insights into client behaviours (organizationally and individually) and what this means in terms of client relationship management; • Understanding the client; • Impact of culture on client relationships and business growth; • Strategic Client relationships and business growth; • Confidence in leading the client - exhibiting a solution-focused approach, being directional, and how to present oneself when negotiating; • Managing conflicts; • Innovative and value-adding client relationships; • Managing leadership of the client across the firm.

title: Reflective Practice
description: This module equips students to critically engage with reflective practice and the integration of their learning from the programme with their professional practice as coaches. There is a particular focus upon the personal development that is required to work effectively with the psychological dimension of coaching.

title: Fin Rep Analysis & Mgmt (10CR)
description: This module is designed to enable participants to understand and interpret financial data and reports in order to operate effectively in a commercial environment. It also provides an understanding of how law firm’s financial performance is measured and managed. This module will cover the following themes- • Understanding and interpreting financial statements;  How Accounting works  The Balance Sheet  The Income Statement  The Statement of Cash Flows  Firm valuations • Financial Statement analysis  The Annual Report - understanding non-financial measures of performance;  Analytical techniques – trend and ratio analysis • Understanding macroeconomic risk  impact of GDP, FX, interest rate and commodity price risks; • The Irish economy  Irish fiscal policy  Brexit • Finance and the Law Firm  Evaluating law firm performance;  Understanding law firm resilience.  Accounting considerations and difficulties in Law Firms

title: Dispute Resolution (10CR)
description: The purpose of this module is to provide participants with a broad understanding of the drivers behind dispute resolution and an understanding of the application and outcomes of the various methods of dispute resolution. This module will cover the following themes- • Psychology and sociology of dispute resolution; • Procedures and techniques of dispute resolution; • Skills required for dispute resolution; • Understanding and analysis of the law and practice applying to different methods of dispute resolution including- • Negotiation • Mediation • Arbitration • Facilitation • Conciliation • Expert Determination. • Crafting of appropriate dispute resolution clauses.

title: Leadership (Uni of Macquarie)
description: The module is designed to provide the fundamental leadership skills and knowledge to enable participants to have a greater impact in their current and future roles, with a strong focus on key skills and insights leaders can immediately apply to improve awareness and effectiveness. The module is a valuable “reality-check” inviting participants to assess current skills and approaches as well as planning for future development.

title: Final Project Presentation
description: The Professional Certificate in Leadership Development consists of seven one- day workshops culminating in the completion of a summative practical project assignment. Upon completion of the programme this project will be presented to the faculty delivering the programme as well as to the senior management team in SEAI. The module will be assessed based on the project presentation and a written submission at the end of the programme. This is a one module 10 ECTS programme. The seven workshops are as follows: • Understanding Our Behaviour as Managers and Leaders • Influencing and Persuasion • Coaching for Executives • Talent Management • Organisational Culture and Change • Strategic Planning • Financial Planning

title: International Consult. Project
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) The International Consulting Project (ICP) sharpens the knowledge, skills, and professional judgement that students have acquired to date on the MBA programme by requiring participants to complete a live consulting project for a client organisation in an international business environment. Due to the intensive timeframe of the module, students are expected to identify the key business issues, engage professionally with the client, conduct focused research and analysis, and develop practical recommendations that are useful to the client organisation. The project requires students to work effectively as a consulting team. Each team member is expected to contribute meaningfully to the development of the engagement scope, the research and analysis process, the formulation of recommendations, and the final client presentation.

title: Business Research Insights
description: This module involves you identifying a worthwhile research topic of clear relevance to the field of international management, undertake a research study related to this topic and present your findings in a clear and impactful manner. To begin with, we will ask you to identify a topic in a broad area of international management that sparks your interest: an unexplained business phenomenon, a novel business practice that may apply more widely than is currently the case, a set of contradictory ideas or business outcomes that require explanation -- anything you would like to understand better and find practical solutions for. This initial choice is critical as you will invest approximately 500 hours of work in your research; it is important to make it worth your time and to enjoy researching something you are truly interested in. You will work on this topic with a partner of your choosing – we know from experience that the end product is much better when there is a partner involved and having a trusted partner on a big task makes it more manageable and fun. Having selected your topic, the next stage will be to review, synthesise and critically analyse the extant literature on this topic with the aim of providing a comprehensive, expert insight into it. While novel insights are not necessarily expected, it is hoped that that you will generate some in the research process. A thoughtful synthesis of dispersed or seemingly contradictory knowledge can be very insightful! The final stage of this research project provides students with the opportunity to demonstrate their ability to identify, collect and analyse data in a systematic manner to produce a unique piece of applied research to add to the extant knowledge on their chosen topic. This part of the project requires you to develop your research skills by completing a piece of research that has relevance to the understanding and practice of international business and to communicate this clearly in a manner accessible to a managerial cohort.

title: Applied Projects OGA (a)
description: Students develop leadership and management competencies, facilitated through live industry-based assignments, supported through induction sessions, ongiong progress review meetings/coaching, webinars, group sessions, reflective journals, problem-based learning and student presentations and script submissions

title: Prof & Career Dev MKT (a)
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) This module focuses on developing leadership and management potential, facilitated through action learning through live industry-based assignments, supported through webinars, group sessions, reflective journals, problem-based learning and student presentations.

title: Project Management for Executives
description: This module has been developed to bring project management to a group of senior managers who may or may not be delivering projects. The module will look at both the what and the how of project management. Where does project management fit in modern organisations. How does project management fit into the realm of change management? This project management module will have three distinct sections. Initially looking at project management through the lenses of the tools and techniques that are used to deliver within the triple constraints of Quality, Time and Cost. The second lens will be looking at projects in the context of a changing environment and set of requirements. The final lens will be looking at the management and leadership requirements of delivering projects.

title: Decision Making for Strategic Execution
description: This module explores principles and tools for effective decision making and strategy execution. An overwhelming body of research suggests that intuitive and ad hoc approaches to decision making are seriously flawed, and that important decisions should therefore be made methodically, with an awareness of and effort to avoid potential biases. Key elements of this module include decision-making in uncertain and complex conditions, ensuring that organisational decision processes are effective, setting goals and motivating people to achieve them, effective feedback principles for reaching those goals, and creative problem solving.

title: Competitive Advantage through Operations
description: This module examines the challenges of managing operations and shows how operational excellence can be a source of competitive advantage. It introduces the basic concepts behind operations management and addresses the strategic impact of operations management on a firm’s competitive advantage. It delves into the challenges of maintaining operational excellence as a firm grows and highlights the importance of keeping operational complexity under control. The module is designed to expose participants to basic theory, to management techniques and to a range of scenarios allowing them to understand the concepts behind operations management. This module will also take you into the world of executing strategy at an operating level. You will be introduced to the leadership imperatives inherent in a strategy execution context and you will develop your ability to deal with the common causes of sub-optimal execution. Of particular importance will be appraising the people factor – recognising the need to win the hearts and minds of employees. Through the play of an interactive computerised simulation you will gain a practical appreciation of the operational challenges inherent in executing strategy. You will also consider the implications of the material for your own work context. The course does not require any prior knowledge of operations management. Teaching methods include lectures, case study workshops and business simulations.

title: Maximising Performance Impact
description: Students develop management competencies, facilitated through live industry-based assignments, supported through induction sessions, ongiong progress review meetings/coaching, webinars, and problem-based learning.

title: Professional Impact Project A
description: This professional impact project asks students to apply academic-based business knowledge as well as incompany experience to an applied, real-life business challenge/opportunity. The project is jointly designed and supported by UCD Smurfit School lecturers and the Bord Bia. Students are expected to work in teams and complete the project using the information available to them as well as any other useful sources. Students are expected to manage the process with a high level of autonomy and to use the module coordinator for advice and support as appropriate. The supervision of the projects will vary from project to project but includes a series of regular meetings with the module co-ordinator and regular interaction with the sponsor from Bord Bia.

title: Business Growth through Customer Value Propositions
description: For food and beverage industry leaders, executives, entrepreneurs and investors in Business- to-Business (B2B) markets this module is an opportunity to gain an understanding of the unique nature of customer value propositions in B2B markets and to gather leading-edge knowledge that they can immediately apply to their work. Business-to-business food and beverage markets are very different to consumer markets: fewer customers, value determined by usage, greater levels of customization, high value sales and purchases often made by groups rather than individuals. Against this background executives in B2B markets are faced with many challenges today as they seek to grow sales profitably, four appear to be most important. First, it is difficult to understand the value that customers wish to buy and then communicate this value to them. Second, it is challenging to selling value in the face of ever-increasing pressure from buyers to reduce price paid. Third, segmenting markets based on value and extracting that value is a challenge. Finally, many firms are challenged by the need to align resources to best secure value from existing marketing activities. This module will address each of these issues and provide practical and actionable solutions drawn from the best thinking of value thinking and customer value proposition development in marketing research.

title: Delivering new opportunities for growth for food business
description: STRATEGIC MARKETINGThe Art and Craft of Playing toWinProfessor Kamran KashaniIntroductionMarkets are not what they used to be. They werestable, slowly evolving and, for the most part, changes in customer behavior and competitive dynamics were gradual and even predictable. Today’s markets are different. Customers are changing faster than many companies can catchupwith them.They are better informed,less loyalandin the driver’s seat. Newcompetitorsarmed with more compelling consumeroffers and better prices disrupt an industry’swell-establishedrules of the game. Winning in the marketplace has never been so demanding.Managers are increasingly aware thatstandstill is not an option, and that if theyare not constantly driving the wavesof change in their sector, through innovation, new business models or simply better consumerexperience, their businesseswill surely becomevictims of changes driven by rivals. Managersare also discovering that future belongs to companies that spot and exploitmarketopportunities early with winning strategies before the emerging trendsbecomeself-evident.In such a dynamic context, the role of marketing is changing. It is changingfrom short-term tacticsto medium-andlong-term strategies; from being preoccupied with a brand’s seasonal or annual promotional campaigns, for example,to identifying the customers’ unmet needs and defining a broadset of strategic decisions that aim to fulfill those needsbetter, faster and more profitably than competitors. In a few words, strategic marketing is playingto win in challengingmarkets.Thismodule is devoted to topics in building and honing marketingstrategies that are built on market insights that exploitexisting oremerging opportunities with adifferentiating advantage.More specifically, through a combination of international case studies, presentations and exerciseswe exploremarketing strategies, their structure and components; view methods to gain actionable insightsinto customer needs and priorities; examine the qualities of strongbrands; and practice makingstrategic marketing decisions.Themodule covers the following essential elements of the programlisted in the ITT: market entry for new products, development/expansion strategies, strategies for growth, building and leveraging brands for growth. Also covered are the following desirable elements of the program listed in the ITT: pricing and costing, innovation, and new market offerings

title: Effective go to Market Strategy for Global Food Business
description: M odule 5–Mastering Route to MarketIn some business settings, the term ‘Route to Market’ has often been limited to describing the set of decisions the business makes around how to physically get their product to their chosen market.This module will explore how the Route to Market choices a business makes can be seen as much broader than just those related to decisions around distribution models. Together and individually, we will focus on the most topical questions that firms need addresswhen evaluating or designing their Route to Market strategy. It will use a series of podcast-based case studies to examine the choices that some UK and Irish food and beverage companies are making

title: Aligning Buyers and Sellers for Effective Customer Account Management
description: It is critically important for suppliers to the retail and foodservice sector, in light of Brexit and other global challenges, to build successful customer relationships. This module will provide students with the necessary tools to implement an organisational structure for strategic customer management in these areas, placing particular emphasis on how FMCG sales and marketing can be integrated to maximum effect. It will also allow students to position their own skills and expertise in relation to a strategic customer management initiative. At the end of the module students should be able to demonstrate their understanding of how the supply chain functions from an account management perspective, differentiate between sales and account management, and be able to link account management to the organisational structure.

title: Prof & Career Dev MKT (b)
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) This module focuses on developing leadership and management potential, facilitated through action learning through live industry-based assignments, supported through webinars, group sessions, reflective journals, problem-based learning and student presentations.

title: Applied Projects MKT (a)
description: Student develop leadership and management competencies, facilitated through live industry-based assignments, supported through induction sessions, ongoing progress review meetings/coaching, webinars, group sessions, reflective journals, problem-based learning and student presentations and script submissions

title: Applied Projects MKT (b)
description: Students develop leadership and management competencies, facilitated through live industry-based assignments, supported through induction sessions, ongiong progress review meetings/coaching, webinars, group sessions, reflective journals, problem-based learning and student presentations and script submissions

title: Coaching in Organisations
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) The module equips students to apply the theory of coaching to the workplace. It presents approaches to key issues of practice, such as contracting, supervision, organisational dynamics and ethics. On completion of the module, students should be able to manage contracting in organisational settings, manage complex organisational dynamics, understand and work appropriately with ethical issues and with issues of difference and diversity.

title: Systemic Coaching and Supervision
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) This module provides participants with a full day of applying leadership theory to coaching. This module also provides participants with a full group coaching supervision session as well as coach practice. On completion of this module participants should be able to apply their learning and skills to senior leaders, manage complex organisational dynamics and be fully engaged with coaching supervision.

title: Gestalt and the Process of Change in Business Coaching
description: This module provides participants with an introduction to the coaching psychology of Gestalt and to behavioural change models to support their coaching sessions. On completing the module participants will be familiar with Gestalt coaching and with a number of change models and how they can be used in coaching. This module is evaluated by a graded coaching exercise on day three of the workshop.

title: CreativeApproaches BusCoaching
description: Provides participants with an understanding of the creative approaches to coaching and covers key areas such as identifying your coaching agenda, coach practice, group supervision and coaching demonstrations.

title: PsychologicalDimensionCoaching
description: Addresses key areas including the psychological dimension of coaching; the four dimensions of a coaching session (anxiety, threat, self-protection, self and relationship management), the Gestalt approach, emotional intelligence and group supervision.

title: Getting Started in BusCoaching
description: This module provides participants with a critical understanding of the theory of and principles of coach contracting and coaching models. On completion of the module participants should be able to describe and critically evaluate key theories and principles of coaching, contract skillfully with clients and apply the theories of coaching. The module is evaluated by a 2,000-word essay comparing two coaching models.

title: Your Smurfit School Information 2022/23
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) Key school information for incoming students in the Smurfit Business School.

title: CEMS Study Abroad
description: Completion of mandatory term abroad at CEMS partner school

title: CEMS Skills Seminar
description: Completion of Mandatory skills seminars for CEMS MIM degree

title: CEMS Introduction Seminar
description: Completion of introduction to UCD CEMS programme

title: Collaborative Communications
description: This module will focus on building trust, connection and collective effectiveness between colleagues, teams and organisations. The work is underpinned by Gestalt theory, aspects of the theory of High-Performance Teams (HPT) and Marshall Rosenberg’s Nonviolent Communication framework. Gestalt, the foundation of best-in-class organisational development and coaching programmes, provides a robust approach to relationality while Nonviolent Communication provides a structure that is supportive and pragmatic enabling participants to make real changes in their listening and communication. The overarching focus is to bring a more relational approach to your teams and groups. On the first day, we will introduce Patrick Lencioni’s theories of High-Performance Teams to discover what are your strengths and growing edges in your teams and leadership. The key concepts are introduced by experiential structures in dyads, triads and groups using a minimum of theory. Nonviolent Communication represents a paradigm shift in communication so experiencing the effect of this approach is key. The second day will concentrate on practical applications. We will show how you can empower your effectiveness to help you build deeper, more effective connections.

title: Data, Artificial Intelligence and Analytics
description: The broad objective of this module is to give participants the knowledge, tools, and insights to demystify AI and analytics, and explore their potential in organizations, particularly in the context of digital transformation. Real-world examples will be presented to demonstrate the capabilities of, the limitations of, and opportunities provided by these technologies. Participants in the module also will discover how to leverage these technologies to create a competitive edge for their business and learn how to anticipate trends and outcomes and make informed decisions. Importantly, participants will explore what it takes for success with AI and analytics and the critical role of information. The module will also address the ethical considerations for AI (fairness, transparency, accountability, etc.); the regulatory landscape for AI (GDPR, CCPA, etc.), and best practices for ethical AI development and deployment.

title: Demand and Supply Chains Applications
description: The focus of this module is to explore the application of digital technologies across demand and supply chains and the wider “connected” ecosystem. The objective is to expose students to a variety of organizational contexts and application areas, and to surface commonalities that provide valuable learnings. These will include digital marketing, financial applications, and deploying technology in operations and the supply chain. The module will also introduce tools to aid in the process of identifying and analyzing potential applications, such as process mapping and customer journey mapping. These will become part of the tool kit of digital transformation, particularly for building the digital strategy.

title: Digital Innovation and Strategy
description: Many companies prioritize innovation as the primary driver of significant growth. However, senior leaders recognize that effectively managing innovation is a complex undertaking, posing challenges for many organizations. To enhance their innovative capabilities, companies must embark on a strategic journey to establish the requisite framework consisting of appropriate mindsets and capabilities. This module offers guidance on developing your innovation framework to facilitate this journey. Innovation encompasses various facets across the organization, including digital innovation in products, services, experiences, channels, processes, and entire business models. Central to this endeavor is cultivating the right mindsets—the amalgamation of thoughts, feelings, and behaviors—among stakeholders to drive innovation and organizational transformation forward. While processes provide the structure for innovation, it is ultimately people who drive its execution. At the heart of digital transformation lies innovation, which drives the creation of new or enhanced products, services, processes, customer experiences, and business models through the integration of digital technologies. Innovations not only inform an organization's digital strategy but also uncover both operational and strategic opportunities. This module begins by examining innovation fundamentals, the innovation process, and essential tools and frameworks. It then delves into the content and methodology of digital strategy to outline a guiding framework. Additionally, the module explores strategies for fostering an innovation ecosystem within the organization, collaborating with startups, incubating ideas, and scaling innovations.

title: Leading Digital Business Transformation
description: Previous modules have explored the capabilities of digital technologies and the strategic and operational opportunities they offer organizations. We have seen that technology challenges traditional industry structures and competitiveness. Additionally, we examined how technology enables organizations to rethink their business models and value propositions, as well as reimagine the delivery of products, services, and customer experiences. We also studied innovation and its role in the digital strategy process. We saw how embracing data and digital tools pushes leaders to reorganize for greater agility and responsiveness to changing customer demands. However, leveraging these opportunities and delivering real business value requires significant organizational change—this is the transformation element of digital transformation. This module tackles the translation of ambition into concrete implementation plans. However, this is against the backdrop where most organizations have struggled with their technology investments. The failure rate of IT projects has remained stubbornly high over the decades. Moreover, research reveals that achieving expected outcomes from digital transformation can be elusive. In today's rapidly evolving business landscape, the ability to navigate and lead digital transformation is crucial for an organization's success and sustainability. How can an organization set up its transformation programme to increase its likelihood of achieving the outcomes it expects?

title: What Digital Means for Strategy, Structure and Competition
description: In setting the scene for this diploma, the central role of data and how it is leveraged will be center stage in this first module. It will emphasize that digital transformation is not just about adopting new technologies; it’s about reimagining business processes and the work of organizations, considering new digital business models, enhancing customer experiences, driving innovation, and leveraging data. These topics will be covered in depth in the remaining modules. The broad question to be addressed in this module is What are the implications of digital technologies for an organization's competitive strategy? The module will explore the impact that digital technologies are having on competition, and how the traditional boundaries between industries and sectors are being blurred. It will examine how digital technologies are affecting the traditional levers of strategy as well as how it is rendering competitive advantage temporary. It will emphasize that organizations cannot ‘opt out’ of considering technology when developing their strategy as, today, digital is a competitive necessity. As many traditional manufacturers shift from selling products to providing services, new digital business models will be studied. In particular, the module will examine platform businesses that are at the heart of innovative business models, the creator economy, and end-to-end visibility for supply chains, supporting new opportunities, marketplaces, and growth.

title: Architecting the Organisation for Digital
description: The capabilities of digital technologies provide the opportunity to re-imagine the concept of an organization and how we arrange people for work. Indeed, digital technologies challenge the very essence of industrial organization, hierarchy, and bureaucracy, which have dominated thinking for many decades. The module explores the purpose of organizing, the role of structure, and present the fundamental principles of organization design and architecture. In today’s digital-first world, the limitations of contemporary organizing models will be investigated, particularly their impact on agility, and newer models will be presented. The fundamental building blocks of a digital enterprise will be presented. The module will examine how pioneers are organizing and managing in a fundamentally different way than most organizations. The utility of the IT department will also be questioned. The module will draw out lessons and insights from pioneering organizations such as Amazon, Spotify, Otto, DPG Media, Starling Bank, DBS Bank, Haier, Enel, Automattic, W.L. Gore, and ING Bank. The important role of culture will be stressed, and what having a digital mindset really means in practice.

title: MBA LEAP
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) The Leadership and Employability Advancement Programme (LEAP) module is designed to provide a structured and integrated approach to career and leadership development for MBA students. The module is intended to improve readiness for the employment market though participation in a series of seminars, masterclasses, workshops, guest lectures, field trips, and an assessment centre. The module is underpinned by the MBA LEAP Employability Framework focused on six behavioral competences measured across four levels. The competences include adaptability; communication and influencing; critical thinking and innovation; inclusive leadership; teamwork and collaboration; and results delivery. Using a combination of psychometric instruments, follow-up coaching, and participation in leadership development activities, the module aims to better equip students with the self-awareness to make career-related decisions. The module comprises a planned set of activities and initiatives that span the entire programme of study. Active engagement in all module activities is mandatory.

title: Executive LEAP
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) The Leadership and Employability Advancement Programme (LEAP) module is designed to provide a structured and integrated approach to career and leadership development for EMBA students. The module is intended to improve readiness for career advancement though participation in a series of seminars, masterclasses, workshops, guest lectures, field trips, and an assessment centre. The module is underpinned by the MBA LEAP Employability Framework focused on six behavioral competences measured across four levels. The competences include adaptability; communication and influencing; critical thinking and innovation; inclusive leadership; teamwork and collaboration; and results delivery. Using a combination of psychometric instruments, follow-up coaching, and participation in leadership development activities, the module aims to better equip students with the self-awareness to make career-related decisions, whether advancement within their existing roles/organisation or entry into new roles/organisations. The module comprises a planned set of activities and initiatives that span the entire programme of study. Active engagement in all module activities is mandatory.

title: Capstone Project MBA
description: The capstone project is a key element of the MBA programme, requiring students to work as a team to complete a live business project for an organisation. Project teams work with the organsation to (i) agree the project scope, (ii) carry out a preliminary analysis, and (iii) develop appropriate, effective solutions. By identifying a solution to a real problem faced by an organization, teams have the opportunity to improve their analytical, diagnostic, communication and relationship-management skills. As most business problems require solutions that draw on a variety of different business disciplines, these projects help students master the practical challenge of integrating and applying the diverse streams of knowledge acquired during their MBA studies. The Capstone Projects are sourced by the Module Coordinator, who also allocates the teams based on student preferences and skill sets.

title: Capstone Project EMBA
description: At the end of the MBA Programme, the capstone project gives participants the chance to broaden their horizons and put into practice the theoretical learning they have acquired. In practice, challenges rarely confine themselves to one functional area but often transcend several parts of the organisation. Therefore, successful managers must be able to tackle complex problems by blending knowledge and skills from the different functional areas. The Capstone Project is, therefore, intended to bring together elements from the entire MBA experience in one final challenge. Before the project start date, participants will engage in various workshops to support the project process, such as Research Methods and Consulting Skills. The projects take place in Spring and Summer. They can be undertaken individually or in groups; however, we encourage participants to work in groups of 3-4. The projects must result in a final written report, which will be submitted to the Programme Office by the agreed-upon deadline.

title: The Manager as Leader
description: This module is designed to equip participants with the essential leadership theory, knowledge and skills needed to drive organisational success and motivate their teams to perform at their best. The module begins by exploring leadership as it relates to today's work environment, the role of a leader in modern organisations, examining the qualities that make a successful leader, and the different leadership styles that can be employed to achieve specific outcomes. Participants will also learn how to develop a leadership style that aligns with their personal values and organizational objectives. Participants will be encouraged to reflect on their own leadership practices, identifying areas for improvement, and developing strategies for enhancing their leadership capabilities. Additionally, participants are encouraged to reflect on the leadership style prevalent in their workplace and critically evaluate how this style impacts on organisational performance.

title: Professional Impact Project B
description: This professional impact project asks students to apply academic-based business knowledge as well as incompany experience to an applied, real-life business challenge/opportunity. The project is jointly designed and supported by UCD Smurfit School lecturers and the Bord Bia. Students are expected to work in teams and complete the project using the information available to them as well as any other useful sources. Students are expected to manage the process with a high level of autonomy and to use the module coordinator for advice and support as appropriate. The supervision of the projects will vary from project to project but includes a series of regular meetings with the module co-ordinator and regular interaction with the sponsor from Bord Bia.

title: The Sustainable Food Business
description: Through this module, we will look at the drivers of the sustainable business movement, who are the key stakeholders, and how sustainability is now expanding into every core function. We will look at examples of the new sustainable business models now emerging. We will examine efforts to date, where the gaps remain, and explore greenwashing and how it materialises. We will gain an understanding of how businesses embed sustainability throughout their value chain and how they engage their stakeholders. We will study the evolution and direction of travel of sustainability policies, regulations, and stakeholder expectations.

title: Digital Marketing for GFB
description: The Internet has dramatically affected consumer behaviour and the way companies interact with and market to consumers. To succeed, companies need marketers with up- to-date knowledge of how to navigate the digital space. This course aims to provide the theoretical knowledge and practical insights for integrating digital marketing into the marketing mix, understanding and engaging online consumers, and monitoring and measuring the results of these efforts.

title: Food S-Chain; Log and Sustain
description: This module considers how distribution trends in the food industry are impacting the ability of Irish firms to sustainably compete in international food markets. Particular emphasis is placed upon practical understanding of how supply chain management decisions determine success and profitability in international markets. Reflecting the role and importance of Origin Green and sustainable supply chains to the Irish food industry, sustainability will be explored in particular. Based on a combination of lectures (both synchronous and asynchronous), in class discussions and case studies, participants will gain a deeper understanding of how the management of the supply chain determines organizational success.

title: Prof & Career Dev OGA
description: Pass/Fail (GPA Neutral) Reflection is the essential link between past action and more effective future action. Learning from experience can be enhanced through deliberate attention to this relationship (McGill and Beaty). The Bord Bia talent programmes delivered by UCD Smurfit Executive Development have had a hugely positive impact on the Irish food industry since 2009. While delivering valuable strategic market insights and opportunities for growth, supporting our participants in achieving their career ambitions is the central driving force for all programme activities. This module has been designed to address the specific professional and career development needs of our Bord Bia MSc participants. In a considerably challenging global context, careful preparation for industry has never been more important. This requires participants to have a clear understanding of the current needs and priorities of Irish food industry employers; to respond by building high performance capabilities in line with the challenges and career pathway opportunities that exist; to build self-awareness to leverage strengths and mitigate weaknesses; to develop an actionable career plan; and to know how to navigate the transition to industry successfully.

title: Developing, Managing & Financing Effective Sustainability Plans
Foundations in AI and Business Analytics
description: The broad objective of this module is to give participants the knowledge, tools, and insights to demystify AI and analytics, and to start to explore their potential in organizations. Real-world examples will be presented to demonstrate the capabilities of, the limitations of, and opportunities provided by these technologies. Participants in the module also will discover how to leverage these technologies to create a competitive edge for their business and learn how to anticipate trends and outcomes and make informed decisions. Importantly, participants will explore what it takes for success with AI and analytics and the critical role of information.

title: How to Leverage AI & Analytics
description: The broad objective of this module is to explore how organizations can effectively and repeatedly leverage AI and analytics for success. We will explore what are the ingredients required to successfully leverage AI & Business Analytics. We will discuss and get hands on with how we might approach augmenting existing business processes with processes for AI & business analytics including alignment to strategy. We will explore how to apply analytics and AI to existing business processes. We will also get hands on and discuss the importance of communication through visual analytics and storytelling with data. In addition, we continue to give participants the knowledge, tools, and insights to demystify AI and analytics, and explore their potential in organizations.

title: Demystifying Business Analytics
description: The broad objective of this module is to explore different facets of Business Analytics (BA) and discuss how and why the BA tools presented are relevant to organizations. The module is split into two parts. The former starts with data, progresses with descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, regression and ends with forecasting; the latter introduces Operational Research (OR), focuses on optimization, complements this with stakeholder involvement technique(s) and ends with a wrap-up and an assessment-related session. We will get hands on with MS Excel during some of the sessions. Some sessions require pre-reading while others will work around a quick case on the day. We may have some guest speakers for some of the sessions. The ultimate goal is to widen the knowledge, tools, and insights to demystify BA tools and explore their potential in organizations.

title: Demystifying Artificial Intelligence Technology
description: This module seeks to equip participants with a comprehensive introduction to artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, focusing on how AI can be leveraged to solve business challenges. The course breaks down complex AI concepts, terminologies, and tools in an accessible and engaging way, providing practical, real-world insights into how AI can inform business operations. Throughout the module participants will explore key topics, including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing (NLP), reinforcement learning, and MLOps (Machine Learning Operations). Through real-life examples and case studies, they will learn how these technologies can drive innovation, improve decision-making, and create competitive advantages in areas in business and industry.

title: Introduction to Aviation Financing and Leasing
description: The aviation finance and leasing industry is unique in Dublin. A leading financial industry with a large front office, providing financial services to companies globally. This module will introduce the industry, provide context with respect to the different skills associated with the industry and detail the financial instruments used by the industry. The aviation sector is heavily dependent on capital markets and financial assets to finance and manage their activities, whether it is the purchase of aircraft using bond financing or the hedging of risks such as oil and currencies. We will explain the main types of financial securities, namely, equities, bonds, and derivative products and how they can be used in aviation.

title: Assets and Markets for Aviation
description: MODULE DESCRIPTION The risks facing the aviation sector are explored through analysis of macroeconomic and firm level risks, where the focus is on managing these risks, to increase the value of the firm. The operations of the markets on which the aviation sector operate are outlined and details on whether they are efficient, and how this impacts on prices of aviation assets. We are particularly interested in aviation stocks. Applications of portfolio theory are outlined in conjunction with asset pricing models, the famous Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), but also other models such as the Chen, Roll and Ross and the Fama-French 3 factor models. We will develop a model of pricing an airline stock. We will examine the use of derivatives of relevance to aviation companies, with a focus on hedging risk.

title: Aircraft Finance and Leasing
description: MODULE DESCRIPTION This module focuses on the mechanisms used to allow aviation borrowers to obtain funds at rates which are economic. Focus will be on credit enhancement, both at the asset and liability level. The module will examine the business models of lessors and how this influences their choice of funding. The various dimensions of credit enhancement will be discussed, allowing borrowers to obtain capital at rates fair below their implied credit quality. Building on this, the sources of financing available to lessors will be developed. Finally, the central role of the aircraft used as collateral will be considered, along with the drivers of aircraft values.

title: Advanced Aviation Financing
description: MODULE DESCRIPTION This module will deal with the most pressing issue faced by aviation, how to decarbonize the industry. Participants will learn about the current challenge, the technologies available and the central role that the financial industry plays in decarbonization. Other important topics will include bank lending, airline credit risk and credit rating assessment. The ‘Runway to Leadership’ session will provide candidates with guidance regarding the ways in which they can accelerate their careers in aviation finance and leasing.

title: Negotiation Strategies for Aviation Finance and Leasing
description: MODULE DESCRIPTION, AND RELATION OF MODULE TO OVERALL PROGRAMME OF STUDY This module equips participants with both the practical skills and theoretical understanding required to be a better negotiator, applied to the context of aviation finance and leasing – and beyond. It presents a systematic approach to negotiation, with a particularly strong focus on creating value and claiming an attractive share of that value at the negotiation table. Participants will acquire skills and tools for defending their interests and achieving their goals through successful negotiation, whether with customers, suppliers, partners, colleagues, or other parties.

title: Corporate Finance for Aviation
description: MODULE DESCRIPTION Commercial airlines depend extensively on the use of capital markets to fund aircraft deliveries. We will examine alternative ways of valuing aviation assets, such as leases. We will use financial statement analysis to assess the performance of an airline company and compare it to its peers, and its trends over time. We assess the relative merits of different sources of finance that an aviation firm, manufacturers, lessors of airlines, can use to support their activities. The section will examine financial decision making in aviation and how firms can make optimal decisions. We will detail the use of investment appraisal techniques such as Net Present Value (NPV). We will examine decision making in an international setting evaluating alternative investment opportunities.

title: Appl'd Sustainable SCM Anlytcs
description: This module is designed to explain and evaluate current thinking in supply chain operations management. Participants will gain a strategic understanding of sustainable operations and be able to apply theories and concepts in a practical setting. The module will review operations management skills and techniques and will introduce the concepts and methods that are useful in understanding sustainable operations management.

title: Sustainable Ops Management
description: This module is designed to explain and evaluate current thinking in supply chain operations management. Participants will gain a strategic understanding of sustainable operations and be able to apply theories and concepts in a practical setting. The module will review operations management skills and techniques and will introduce the concepts and methods that are useful in understanding sustainable operations management.

title: Foundations of Sustainable SCM
description: This module develops participants’ understanding of sustainable supply chain management. Participants will be introduced to the core supply chain functions of operations, purchasing, and logistics. They will also develop technical expertise in supply chain sustainability concepts and will begin to explore how supply chain decisions contribute to the organization’s economic, environmental and social outcomes.

title: Applied Projects OGA (b)
description: Applied Projects will help you gain fundamental expertise in business sustainability and the global food, drink and horticulture industry. The module is based on action learning, a process of continuous practice, reflection and enhanced knowledge and capability. It allows you to gain in-depth knowledge of the emerging issues facing the international food industry; capture strategically valuable insights, and share these insights and opportunities to support key decision makers representing Irish food companies with the highest growth potential. The MSc in Business Sustainability facilitates learning through placements with the world’s leading organisations. During the programme, you will meet and network with a wide range of industry leaders, functional experts and governmental agencies to help you foster real links in industry. Applied Projects will facilitate your learning from your placement experiences complemented by in-class modules. As a participant you are expected to evolve into an industry expert with the ability to advise and manage change and to help the organisation respond effectively to related strategic challenges.

title: Leadership (AGSM @ UNSW)
description: Individual coaching and mentoring are part of the Godolphin Flying Start experience. A blend of workshops and Myers Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) is used to develop personal awareness as a foundaton for leadership development. A Leadership module is completed at the Australian Graduate School of Management.

title: Professional Impact Project B
description: The Professional Impact Project creates a unique opportunity for students to explore the intersection of business and their knowledge from the classroom to a food company working on a real-life business challenge. The project, based on contributing to Bord Bia strategy, is jointly designed and supported by UCD Smurfit School lecturers and Bord Bia. Students are expected to work in teams and complete the project using the information available to them as well as any other useful sources. Students are expected to manage the process with a high level of autonomy and to use the module coordinator for advice and support as appropriate. The supervision of the projects will vary from project to project but includes a series of regular meetings with the module co-ordinator and regular interaction with the sponsor from Bord Bia.

title: Digital Marketing for GFB
description: The explosion of new technologies have transformed customer behaviour and disrupted global marketplaces. As a result, marketing practices must also evolve. Digital Marketing for Global Food Business is a strategic-level course in planning and implementing international business using digital technology. The module will consider how to better align your marketing efforts with today’s digital-savvy customer through an introduction to digital-centric customer behaviours. It will explore how businesses are evolving their marketing by incorporating data and analytics techniques for improved decision-making. Using case studies, it will explore companies that are using new marketing technologies to better equip their marketing and gain organizational efficiencies.

title: Food S-Chain; Log and Sustain
description: This module considers how distribution trends in the food industry are impacting the ability of Irish firms to sustainably compete in international food markets. Particular emphasis is placed upon practical understanding of how supply chain management decisions determine success and profitability in international markets. Reflecting the role and importance of Origin Green and sustainable supply chains to the Irish food industry, sustainability will be explored in particular. Based on a combination of lectures, in class discussions and case studies, participants will gain a deeper understanding of how the management of the supply chain determines organizational success.

title: MKTG: Insight-Impact Food Mkt
description: Marketing is a mindset. It is a way of looking at the world that is customer-focused, insight-driven and ever-changing. It begins long before products and services reach the market and continue long after they have been delivered. It is ultimately about creating, defining, and delivering value to the customer in a profitable and sustainable way for the customer and the business. This module recognises that success in global markets has never been more difficult to achieve. To thrive and flourish in this environment, businesses must develop differentiated products and services based on sound customer insights, enhancing their ability to deliver products and services to the market with impact.

title: Dev Cust Insight–Prod InnovGFB
description: A customer-led organisation really searches for new ways to solve customer problems and create value through better product innovations, not what’s already established by their competitors in the market. Central to this customer focus is a strong belief in insights, and in the active use of a diverse mix of insight tools—new and old, qualitative and quantitative, digital and analogue— to get better answers. This module will introduce students to the variety of tools that can be used to uncover insights, understand how to test these insights and leverage them to capture and deliver real innovative value. Specifically, we look into the role of AI in generating and analysing customer insights throughout the innovation process.

title: Bus Growth - Cust Value Prop
description: For food and beverage industry leaders, executives, entrepreneurs and investors in Business- to-Business (B2B) markets this module is an opportunity to gain an understanding of the unique nature of customer value propositions in B2B markets and to gather leading-edge knowledge that they can immediately apply to their work. Business-to-business food and beverage markets are very different to consumer markets: fewer customers, value determined by usage, greater levels of customization, high value sales and purchases often made by groups rather than individuals. Against this background executives in B2B markets are faced with many challenges today as they seek to grow sales profitably, four appear to be most important. First, it is difficult to understand the value that customers wish to buy and then communicate this value to them. Second, it is challenging to selling value in the face of ever-increasing pressure from buyers to reduce price paid. Third, segmenting markets based on value and extracting that value is a challenge. Finally, many firms are challenged by the need to align resources to best secure value from existing marketing activities. This module will address each of these issues and provide practical and actionable solutions drawn from the best thinking of value thinking and customer value proposition development in marketing research.

title: The Sustainable Food Business
description: The aim of this module is to provide students with a deep foundational knowledge of the theories and practice of business sustainability. While once a nice to have, sustainability has now become a core requirement for organisations across all industries and sectors. Through this module, we will look at the drivers of the sustainable business movement, who are the key stakeholders, and how sustainability is now expanding into every core function. We will look at examples of the new sustainable business models now emerging using practical examples and case studies to bring this topic to life. We will gain an understanding of how businesses embed sustainability throughout their value chain and how they engage their stakeholders. We will study the evolution and direction of travel of sustainability policies, regulations and stakeholder expectations.

title: Agricultural Science: Closing the Gap on Irish & International Sustainability Goals
Food & Life: Aligning Business, Health, & Pleasure through Nudging
Leading Change for Successful Sustainability Implementation
Accelerating Sustainability through Artificial Intelligence & Digitization
Sustainability & Branding: Creating Commercial Impact for Irish Firms
FutureSustainabilityLeadership
description: A four-seminar series (Dec 2026–Nov 2027) tracing sustainability leadership from vision to execution to legacy, designed to complement placements by exposing participants to real executive decision-making and trade-offs.

title: Professional Impact Project B
description: This professional impact project asks students to apply academic-based business knowledge as well as incompany experience to an applied, real-life business challenge/opportunity. The project is jointly designed and supported by UCD Smurfit School lecturers and the Bord Bia. Students are expected to work in teams and complete the project using the information available to them as well as any other useful sources. Students are expected to manage the process with a high level of autonomy and to use the module coordinator for advice and support as appropriate. The supervision of the projects will vary from project to project but includes a series of regular meetings with the module co-ordinator and regular interaction with the sponsor from Bord Bia.

title: MaximisingPerformance Impact A
description: This capability development module is a pass-fail module running alongside placement and programme activity. It is designed around real professional contribution in live commercial environments, and helps structure and make visible how a participant's professional judgement, commercial reasoning, stakeholder engagement, execution, communication, and ability to adjust develop over time through real organisational work.

title: MaximisingPerformance Impact B
description: This capability development module is a pass-fail module running alongside placement and programme activity. It is designed around real professional contribution in live commercial environments, and helps structure and make visible how a participant's professional judgement, commercial reasoning, stakeholder engagement, execution, communication, and ability to adjust develop over time through real organisational work.

title: Dialogue & Emergence
description: A sample of the content covered for this module is as follows: • Relational approach and Ethical Presence (SOS model) • Phenomenology as foundation for dialogue • Buber’s I-Thou principles and Gestalt cycle of experience • Live team coaching demonstrations • Coach practice with peer supervision • Reflexive inquiry and use of self

title: Diagnostic Debriefs, Relational Foundations & Working with Conflict
description: This module will assist team coaches effectively debrief diagnostic data, cultivate psychological safety, and transform team conflict into productive system insights using frameworks like Thomas-Kilmann.

title: Introduction to Team Coaching and Team Effectiveness & Getting Started: Contracting & Diagnosing
description: This module focuses on the science of team effectiveness to provide participants with an understanding of what constitutes team outcomes, and which processes and inputs have been shown by research to impact team effectiveness. This grounding will assist the team coach in focusing their approach and building rigor and measurement into their work. The importance and complexities of contracting with teams is also explored along with the role of diagnostics as a first key intervention into the team system. Types of team diagnostic approaches will be discussed and key instruments reviewed. A sample of the content which will be covered is as follows: • Team Coaching definitions (Hackman & Wageman, Clutterbuck, Hawkins, Woudstra, Graves etc) • Team effectiveness science & research (Google Project Aristotle, Edmondson) • Teams vs groups distinction • Team types & typographies (Hackman, Tuckman, Clutterbuck, Hawkins) • Psychological safety foundations • Learning group formation • Multi-level contracting (organisational, team, individual) • Ethics and confidentiality frameworks • STOKeRS model (Farmer) • Coach practice with contracting scenarios • Diagnostic approaches & instruments (PERILL, CID-CLEAR, Six Team Conditions) • Diagnostic and dialogic approaches to debriefing • Using data to deepen team awareness
